title: The Bosphorus Brief — October 4, 2026
overview: A quiet Sunday on the ground in Türkiye, though regional tensions and a domestic political storm over a fund crisis dominate headlines. Residents will find practical news on residency processing and currency stability more relevant than the geopolitics playing out around the country's borders.

sections.heading: Residency: Fingerprinting Comes to Campus
sections.body: Good news for international students in Eskişehir: Anadolu University hosted a visit from the Provincial Migration Authority, allowing students to give fingerprints for residence permits without traveling to the Migration office directly. Habertürk confirms this on-campus processing model is being used elsewhere too. If you're a student elsewhere in Türkiye, it's worth asking your international office whether a similar arrangement exists before booking a trip across town for an appointment.

sections.heading: Fund Crisis Draws Political Fire
sections.body: Nationalist MHP leader Devlet Bahçeli described the country's ongoing investment fund turmoil as a 'purification process,' per BBC, Serbestiyet, and NTV Haber. No new regulatory detail accompanied the remark. Separately, Turkey's financial regulators extended the lower margin trading requirement through October 30 (Investing.com) — a technical measure, but one that signals authorities are still managing volatility in equity markets. Residents with brokerage accounts should expect continued caution rather than resolution in the near term.

sections.heading: Headscarf Bans in Azerbaijan: A Notable Silence
sections.body: Turkish Minute (opposition-leaning) reports that Ankara has not publicly addressed new Azerbaijani school dress rules restricting headscarves, despite President Erdoğan's own criticism of headscarf bans at the UN General Assembly weeks earlier. This is a freedom-of-belief story worth watching: so far it has only surfaced in opposition-leaning coverage, with no response yet from state or pro-government outlets. No policy change affects residents in Türkiye directly, but it's a telling gap in messaging consistency on an issue Ankara has previously raised internationally.

sections.heading: Money and Markets: Lira Holds Steady
sections.body: USD/TRY sits at 49.13, EUR/TRY at 55.29 — broadly in line with recent weeks, offering no fresh shocks for budgeting or remittances. The central bank's policy rate trajectory (tracked via Statista back to 2002) remains the backdrop for continued inflation-watching; no rate decision was reported today.

sections.heading: Safety Note: Regional Conflict, Not Local
sections.body: Multiple outlets covered intensifying rhetoric around Iran and Lebanon, plus a flydubai incident involving an alleged attempted hijacking on an Israel-bound flight. None of this touches Türkiye directly — the US travel advisory keeps Türkiye at a steady Level 2, the same as Egypt, while Syria, Iraq, Iran, and Lebanon remain Level 4. If you have travel plans into neighboring countries this month, check current advisories before booking, but day-to-day life in Türkiye is unaffected.

closing: Stay dry if the Bosphorus wind picks up tonight — and as always, we'll keep watching the paperwork so you don't have to.
